paragraphs: Cathay General Bancorp (the "Bancorp" on a parent-only basis, and the "Company," "we," "us" or "our" on a consolidated basis) is a corporation that was organized in 1990 under the laws of the State of Delaware. The Bancorp is the holding company of Cathay Bank, a California state-chartered commercial bank ("Cathay Bank" or the "Bank"), and twelve limited partnerships investing in affordable housing investments in which the Bank is the sole limited partner. The Bancorp also owns 100% of the common stock of five statutory business trusts created for the purpose of issuing capital securities.

Our principal place of business is located at 777 North Broadway, Los Angeles, California 90012, with our main telephone number at (213) 625-4700. Certain of our administrative offices are located at 9650 Flair Drive, El Monte, California 91731. Our common stock is traded on the NASDAQ Global Select Market, and our trading symbol is "CATY".

The Bancorp is regulated as a bank holding company by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System ("Federal Reserve"). Cathay Bank is regulated as a California commercial bank by the California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation ("DFPI") and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation ("FDIC").
At December 31, 2025, we had $24.23 billion in total consolidated assets, $19.94 billion in net loans, $20.89 billion in deposits, and $2.93 billion in shareholders' equity.
In addition to Cathay Bank, the Bancorp has the following subsidiaries:

Cathay Capital Trust I, Cathay Statutory Trust I, Cathay Capital Trust II, Cathay Capital Trust III and Cathay Capital Trust IV. The Bancorp established Cathay Capital Trust I in June 2003, Cathay Statutory Trust I in September 2003, Cathay Capital Trust II in December 2003, Cathay Capital Trust III in March 2007, and Cathay Capital Trust IV in May 2007 (collectively, the "Trusts") as subsidiaries. The Trusts are statutory business trusts. The Trusts issued capital securities representing undivided preferred beneficial interests in the assets of the Trusts. The Trusts exist for the purpose of issuing the capital securities and investing the proceeds thereof, together with proceeds from the purchase of the common securities of the Trusts by the Bancorp, in a certain series of securities issued by us, with similar terms to the relevant series of securities issued by each of the Trusts, which we refer to as "Junior Subordinated Notes." The Bancorp guarantees, on a limited basis, payments of distributions on the capital securities of the Trusts and payments on redemption of the capital securities of the Trusts. The Bancorp is the owner of all the beneficial interests represented by the common securities of the Trusts. The purpose of issuing the capital securities was to provide the Company with a cost-effective means of obtaining capital. Because the Bancorp is not the primary beneficiary of the Trusts, the financial statements of the Trusts are not included in our Consolidated Financial Statements.

The Bancorp's primary business is to act as the holding company for the Bank. Accordingly, the Bancorp faces the same competitive pressures as those expected by the Bank. For a discussion of those risks, see "Business of the Bank — Competition" below under this Item 1.

Due to the limited nature of the Bancorp's activities as a bank holding company, the Bancorp currently does not employ any persons other than the Bancorp's corporate officers, which includes the Chief Executive Officer and President, Executive Chairman, the Chief Financial Officer, the Corporate Secretary, General Counsel and Sustainability Officer, and the Assistant Corporate Secretary. See also "Business of the Bank — Employees" below under this Item 1 where we describe human capital management matters for Cathay Bank. In the future, the Bancorp may become an operating company or may engage in such other activities or acquire such other businesses as may be permitted by applicable law.

Cathay Bank was incorporated under the laws of the State of California on August 22, 1961, is licensed by the DFPI, and commenced operations as a California state-chartered bank on April 19, 1962. Cathay Bank is an insured bank under the Federal Deposit Insurance Act by the FDIC, but it is not a member of the Federal Reserve.

The Bank's head office is located in the Chinatown area of Los Angeles, at 777 North Broadway, Los Angeles, California 90012. As of December 31, 2025, the Bank has branch offices in Southern California (24 branches), Northern California (17 branches), New York (9 branches), Washington (four branches), Illinois (two branches), Texas (two branches), Maryland (one branch), Massachusetts (one branch), Nevada (one branch), New Jersey (one branch), and Hong Kong (one branch) and a representative office in Beijing, Shanghai, and Taipei. Deposit accounts at the Hong Kong branch are not insured by the FDIC. Current activities of the Beijing, Shanghai, and Taipei representative offices are limited to coordinating the transportation of documents to the Bank's head office and performing liaison services.

Our primary market area is defined by the CRA delineation, which includes the contiguous areas surrounding each of the Bank's branch offices. It is the Bank's policy to reach out and actively offer services to low-to- moderate income groups in the delineated branch service areas. Many of the Bank's employees speak more than one language, including both English and one or more Chinese dialects or Vietnamese, and are thus able to serve the Bank's English, Chinese and Vietnamese speaking clients.

As a commercial bank, the Bank offers products and services to businesses, such as checking and deposit, lines of credits, commercial and commercial real estate loans, merchant services and payment processing, treasury management services, international banking and financing services, and other customary banking services. The bank offers similar services that are available to consumers.

The Bank primarily services individuals, professionals, and small to medium-sized businesses in the local markets in which its branches are located and provides commercial real estate loans, commercial loans, U.S. Small Business Administration ("SBA") loans, residential mortgage loans, real estate construction loans, home equity lines of credit, and installment loans to individuals for, household and other consumer expenditures.

Through its Cathay Wealth Management business unit, the Bank offers clients a range of investment products and services, such as stocks, bonds, mutual funds, insurance, annuities, and advisory services. As of December 31, 2025, all securities and insurance products provided by Cathay Wealth Management are offered by, and all financial consultants are registered with, Cetera Investment Services LLC, a registered securities broker/dealer and licensed insurance agency and member of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority and Security Investor Protection Corporation. Cetera Investment Services LLC and Cathay Bank are independent entities. The securities and insurance products offered by Cetera Investment Services LLC are not insured by the FDIC.

headings: Risk Factors Summary
Market and Economic Risks
Credit, Interest Rate and Liquidity Risks
Operational Risks
Information, Information Technology and Privacy Risks
Regulatory, Compliance and Legal Risks
Risks Related to Ownership of Our Common Stock
Current unfavorable and uncertain economic and market conditions may adversely affect our industry and business.
Economic conditions in California and the other markets in which we operate may adversely affect our business.
Our loan portfolio is largely secured by real estate, and a downturn in the real estate market may adversely affect our results of operations.
Adverse conditions in Asia and elsewhere could adversely affect our business.
The soundness of other financial institutions could adversely affect us.
We may be required to make additional provisions for loan losses and charge off additional loans in the future, which could adversely affect our results of operations.
The allowance for credit losses is an estimate of expected credit losses. Actual credit losses in excess of the estimate could adversely affect our results of operations and capital.
Our business is subject to interest rate risk, and fluctuations in interest rates could reduce our net interest income and adversely affect our business.
Inflation and deflation may adversely affect our financial performance.
Liquidity risk could impair our ability to fund operations and jeopardize our financial condition.
If the Company's goodwill were determined to be impaired, it would result in a charge against earnings and thus a reduction in stockholders' equity.
We may incur significant losses as a result of ineffective risk management processes and strategies.
Concentration of risk increases the potential for significant losses.
Our commercial loan, commercial real estate loan and construction loan portfolios expose us to risks that may be greater than the risks related to our other loans.
Our investments and/or financings in certain tax-advantaged projects may not generate returns as anticipated and may have an adverse impact on our financial results.
Our use of appraisals in deciding whether to make a loan on or secured by real property does not ensure the value of the real property collateral.
Our use of third-party vendors and our other ongoing third-party business relationships are subject to increasing regulatory requirements and attention.
Our deposit insurance premiums could increase in the future, which could have a material adverse impact on future earnings and financial condition.
As we expand our business outside of California markets, including through acquisitions, we may encounter additional risks that could adversely affect our business and earnings.
We face substantial competition from our competitors.
We are dependent on key personnel and the loss of one or more of those key personnel may materially and adversely affect our prospects.
Natural disasters, geopolitical events, public health crises and other catastrophic events beyond our control could adversely affect us.
Governmental and societal responses to climate change and other environmental impacts could adversely affect our business and performance, including indirectly through impacts on our clients.
paragraphs: Ownership of our common stock involves certain risks. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Understanding these risks is important to understanding any statement in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. You should carefully read and consider the risks and uncertainties described below together with all of the other information included or incorporated by reference in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including under the heading "Management's Discussion and Analysis". Further, to the extent that any of the information in this report, or in other reports we file with the SEC, constitutes forward-looking statements, the risk factors below are cautionary statements identifying important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed in any forward-looking statements made by us or on our behalf. See "Forward-Looking Statements". The risks described below are not the only ones facing our business. Additional risks that management is not aware of or focused on or that management currently deems immaterial may also impair our business operations. This Annual Report on Form 10-K is qualified in its entirety by these risk factors.

If any of the following risks actually occur, our business, financial condition and results of operations could be materially and adversely affected. If this were to happen, the value of our common stock could significantly decline, and you could lose some or all of your investment.

The following is a summary of the material risks that we believe could adversely affect our business, operations and financial results. These risks are discussed more fully below and include, but are not limited to:
Unfavorable or uncertain economic and market conditions, including in California and the other markets in which we operate, can adversely affect our industry and business.
Our loan portfolio is largely secured by real estate, and a downturn in the real estate market may adversely affect our results of operations.
Adverse conditions in Asia and elsewhere could adversely affect our business.

paragraphs: Cathay General Bancorp（於母公司層級稱為 "Bancorp"，於合併層級稱為 "Company"、"we"、"us" 或 "our"）為一於1990年根據德拉華州法律設立之公司。Bancorp為Cathay Bank（一間加州州立發行的商業銀行，稱為 "Cathay Bank" 或 "Bank"）之控股公司，並為十二間投資於可負擔住宅投資之有限合夥企業之投資者，其中Bank為唯一有限合夥人。Bancorp亦擁有五間法定商業信託之100%普通股，該信託設立之目的為發行資本證券。
本公司主要營業據點位於美國加州洛杉磯市北百老匯街777號，郵遞區號90012，主要電話為(213) 625-4700。部分行政辦公室位於加州艾爾蒙特市Flair Drive 9650號，郵遞區號91731。本公司普通股於NASDAQ Global Select Market交易，交易代碼為 "CATY"。
Bancorp由美國聯邦儲備系統（"Federal Reserve"）作為銀行控股公司進行監管。Cathay Bank由加州財政保護與創新部（"DFPI"）及美國存款保險公司（"FDIC"）作為加州商業銀行進行監管。
於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司合併總資產為 24.23 十億美元，淨貸款為 19.94 十億美元，存款為 20.89 十億美元，以及股東權益為 2.93 十億美元。
除Cathay Bank外，Bancorp尚有以下子公司：

Cathay Capital Trust I、Cathay Statutory Trust I、Cathay Capital Trust II、Cathay Capital Trust III及Cathay Capital Trust IV。Bancorp於2003年6月設立Cathay Capital Trust I，2003年9月設立Cathay Statutory Trust I，2003年12月設立Cathay Capital Trust II，2007年3月設立Cathay Capital Trust III，以及2007年5月設立Cathay Capital Trust IV（合稱 "Trusts"）作為子公司。Trusts為法定商業信託。Trusts發行資本證券，代表對Trusts資產之不分割優先受益權益。Trusts設立之目的為發行資本證券，並投資其所得款項，以及由Bancorp購入Trusts普通證券所得款項，於本公司發行之特定系列證券，其條款與各Trusts所發行之相關系列證券相似，我們稱之為 "Junior Subordinated Notes"。Bancorp於有限範圍內擔保支付Trusts資本證券之分派及支付其贖回之款項。Bancorp為Trusts普通證券所代表之所有受益權益之所有者。發行資本證券之目的為為本公司提供一種成本效益之取得資本方式。由於Bancorp並非Trusts之主要受益人，Trusts之財務報表未包含於本公司合併財務報表中。
Bancorp之主要業務為擔任Bank之控股公司。因此，Bancorp所面對之競爭壓力與Bank預期相同。有關這些風險之討論，請參閱本項目1之下 "Bank之業務 — 競爭" 部分。
由於Bancorp作為銀行控股公司之活動範圍有限，目前Bancorp僅僱用其公司高層管理人員，包括首席執行官與總裁、執行主席、首席財務官、公司祕書、總法律顧問與永續發展官，以及助理公司祕書。另請參閱本項目1之下 "Bank之業務 — 員工" 部分，其中我們說明Cathay Bank之人力資本管理事項。未來，Bancorp可能成為營運公司，或進行其他活動或取得其他業務，視適用法律之許可而定。
Cathay Bank 於 1961 年 8 月 22 日根據加利福尼亞州法律設立，並取得 DFPI 許可，於 1962 年 4 月 19 日開始營運為加利福尼亞州特許銀行。Cathay Bank 為根據《美國存款保險法》由 FDIC 保險的銀行，但並非美國聯邦儲備系統成員。

本行總行位於洛杉磯唐人街地區，地址為加利福尼亞州洛杉磯市北 Broadway 街 777 號，郵遞區號 90012。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本行在美國南加州設有 24 處分行，北加州設有 17 處分行，紐約設有 9 處分行，華盛頓設有四處分行，伊利諾設有兩處分行，德州設有兩處分行，馬裏蘭設有一處分行，麻薩諸塞設有一處分行，內華達設有一處分行，新澤西設有一處分行，香港設有一處分行，並在北京、上海及臺北設有代表處。香港分行的存款帳戶並未由 FDIC 保險。北京、上海及臺北代表處目前僅限於協調文件至本行總行的運輸及執行聯絡服務。
我們的主要業務區域為 CRA 劃分的範圍，包含本行各分行周圍的連續區域。本行政策為主動向劃定分行服務區域內低收入至中等收入羣體提供服務。許多本行員工會說多種語言，包括英語及一種或數種中文方言或越南語，因此能為本行英語、中文及越南語客戶提供服務。
作為商業銀行，本行為企業提供產品與服務，例如支票帳戶與存款、信用線、商業與商業不動產貸款、商家服務與付款處理、財務管理服務、國際銀行與融資服務，以及其他常見的銀行服務。本行也提供與消費者相同的服務。
本行主要服務其分行所在地的個人、專業人士及中小型企業，並提供商業不動產貸款、商業貸款、美國小企業管理局（"SBA"）貸款、住宅抵押貸款、不動產建設貸款、住宅貸款信用線及 installment loans 給個人用於家庭及其他消費者支出。

透過其 Cathay Wealth Management 事業單位，本行為客戶提供一系列投資產品與服務，例如股票、債券、共同基金、保險、年金及顧問服務。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，Cathay Wealth Management 提供的所有證券與保險產品均由 Cetera Investment Services LLC 提供，且所有財務顧問均在 Cetera Investment Services LLC 註冊。Cetera Investment Services LLC 為註冊證券經紀商與持有保險代理牌照的機構，並為金融產業監管局及證券投資者保護公司成員。Cetera Investment Services LLC 與 Cathay Bank 為獨立機構。Cetera Investment Services LLC 提供的證券與保險產品並未由 FDIC 保險。

headings: 風險因素總覽
市場與經濟風險
信用、利率與流動性風險
營運風險
資訊、資訊科技與隱私權風險
法規、合規與法律風險
與本公司普通股 ownership 相關的風險
目前不利且不確定的經濟與市場條件可能對我們的產業與業務產生負面影響。
加州及其他我們營運市場的經濟情況可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們的貸款組合主要以不動產為擔保，不動產市場走弱可能對我們的營運結果產生不利影響。
亞洲及其他地區的不利情況可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
其他金融機構的健全性可能對我們產生不利影響。
我們可能需要在未來提列更多貸款減損準備並核銷更多貸款，這可能對我們的營運結果產生不利影響。
貸款減損準備係用以估計預期貸款減損。實際貸款減損若高於預估，可能對我們的營運結果及資本產生不利影響。
我們的業務面臨利率風險，利率波動可能降低我們的淨利息收入，並對我們的業務產生不利影響。
通貨膨脹及通貨緊縮可能對我們的財務表現產生不利影響。
流動性風險可能影響本公司資金運用能力，並危及財務狀況。
若本公司之商譽被認定為減損，將導致對收益之減損，進而降低股東權益。
本公司可能因風險管理程序及策略不當而產生重大損失。
風險集中度增加產生重大損失之潛在可能性。
本公司之營業貸款、營業不動產貸款及建築貸款組合，可能使本公司面臨大於其他貸款相關風險之風險。
本公司對某些稅務優惠項目之投資及/或融資，可能無法達成預期之回報，並可能對財務結果產生負面影響。
本公司於決定是否對不動產提供貸款或以不動產擔保貸款時，使用評估價值之方式，無法確保不動產擔保品之價值。
本公司使用第三方廠商及其它持續進行之第三方商業關係，受日益嚴格之監管要求及關注。
本公司存款保險費率未來可能提高，這可能會對未來獲利及財務狀況產生重大不利影響。
隨著我們拓展業務至加州以外的市場，包括透過收購方式，我們可能會面臨額外風險，這些風險可能對本公司業務及獲利產生不利影響。
本公司面臨來自競爭對手的重大競爭壓力。
本公司依賴關鍵人員，若失去其中一位或多位關鍵人員，可能會對本公司前景產生重大且不利的影響。
天然災害、地緣政治事件、公共衛生危機及其他超出本公司控制範圍的災難性事件，可能會對本公司產生不利影響。
政府及社會對氣候變遷及其他環境影響的應對措施，可能會對本公司業務及表現產生不利影響，包括間接透過對客戶的影響。
paragraphs: 本公司普通股的持有涉及某些風險。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非本公司唯一面臨的風險。瞭解這些風險對理解本年度報告表10-K中任何陳述非常重要。您應仔細閱讀並考慮下列所描述的風險與不確定性，並與本年度報告表10-K中包含或參考的其他資訊一併考量，包括標題為『管理層討論與分析』的部分。此外，若本報告或本公司向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）所提交的其他報告中任何資訊屬於展望性陳述，則下列風險因素為警示性陳述，識別出可能導致實際結果與任何展望性陳述中所表達結果有重大差異的重要因素。請參閱『展望性陳述』。下列所描述的風險並非本公司業務唯一面臨的風險。此外，管理層未察覺或未著重的風險，或管理層目前認為不重要的風險，也可能影響本公司業務運作。本年度報告表10-K全文均受這些風險因素所限定。
若下列任何風險實際發生，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運結果造成重大且不利的影響。若發生此情況，本公司普通股的價值可能顯著下跌，您可能損失部分或全部投資。
下列為本公司認為可能對業務、營運與財務結果造成不利影響的重要風險總結。這些風險在下文中會更詳細討論，包括但不限於：
不利或不確定的經濟與市場條件，包括在加州及其他我們營運的市場，可能對本公司產業與業務造成不利影響。
本公司貸款組合主要以不動產為擔保，不動產市場的衰退可能對本公司營運結果造成不利影響。
亞洲及其他地區的不利條件可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
